title: The case-move answer, the proceeds-fact activity and the source-data product the step needs have no published operation name and no row in the plan dependency lists
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-030, its metadata row Depends on FEAT-PAY-10, its Story paragraph, Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4 and Endpoints); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.21.2 integration points ALS and GL, prerequisites FEAT-PAY-10); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T5.1, T5.2, T5.3, T-A.1); _work/msr/context/S5.md (connection matrix row S5 Asset); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (both slices of RWB-E4-030: H, C, I and X lists)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2, 6 and 8; s5 X4 and X8; s12.2; s12.8; s13; CON s3, s4 step 4, s11 Data, s12.2, s12.8
description: The step is event-started and answers a case, but no source publishes the operation that carries the case move, the activity that returns the proceeds fact, or the data product that replaces the two legacy ACE reads. The legacy story declares its dependency as FEAT-PAY-10 of P8, the FSD repeats that prerequisite and names ALS and GL as its integration points, and the TSD S5 T5.2 describes cross-module calls as published Java interfaces to P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 without naming one. The connection matrix gives S5 Asset a Temporal call to P3 and a Temporal plus event relation with P8, and the architecture notes say route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal and never REST. The plan carries C, I and X as empty lists for both slices, although the legacy dependency crosses a service boundary.
evidence: Legacy metadata: Depends on FEAT-PAY-10. FSD S5 A2.21.2 integration points ALS and GL, prerequisites FEAT-PAY-10. TSD S5 T5.2: calls go through the published Java interfaces, P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices. Context pack connection matrix row S5 Asset: P3 T, S4 E, P8 T E, S9 T E, no R. Plan slices RWB-S5-E4030-APP and RWB-S5-E4030-CON: C, I and X empty.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the owners of P3 rwb-case, P8 rwb-payment and P1 rwb-source-data
proposed: Read the three rows as boundary rows of the platform envelope on day one, build against their documents and fakes, keep the plan C list empty because the pair is a consumed contract and not a build gate, and register the rows in the Service Contract Catalog and the next plan revision.

title: The event catalogue names Case and workflow as the only consumer of ProceedsMatched while Architecture v5 gives S5 an event subscription to P8
source: Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4 (sheet Events, row EV-25, its Consumers column); _work/msr/context/S5.md (connection matrix row S5 Asset and the naming rules); Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 slide 13 (row S5 Asset, column P8)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 step 1; s8 BR8; s12.4; s12.8; s13; CON s3, s7 AC6, s11 Data, s12.4, s12.8
description: Two sources give two consumer lists for one event. The Event and Messaging Design v4 publishes EV-25 ProceedsMatched with Case and workflow as its only consumer and Payload proceedsId, caseId and amount. Architecture v5 slide 13, the connection matrix, marks the S5 Asset row and the P8 column as Temporal plus listens to events, and the slides that name this service describe the asset disposal stage as reacting to the money, including the five-day payment term and the settlement of a sale. Under the source precedence of Template and Rules v1 R3 the catalogue slides rank above the event design, so the subscription holds; the loser is recorded here.
evidence: Event and Messaging Design v4, EV-25 ProceedsMatched, Published, Payments and posting, proceedsId, caseId, amount, Consumers: Case and workflow. Connection matrix row S5 Asset, column P8: T E. Template and Rules v1 R3 source precedence item 1 above item 6.
area: Events and messaging, S5 rwb-asset with P8 rwb-payment
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the owner of the P8 rwb-payment event catalogue row
proposed: Declare the subscription to rwb.payment.events.v1 for EV-25 with the consumer group rwb-asset, keep the envelope, the idempotency key and the retry and .dlt topics of the platform, and ask the event catalogue owner to add rwb-asset to the consumer list at its next version.

title: The legacy data table reads v_ace_account and v_ace_npa_sale while the target gives S5 no edge to rwb-source-data and reserves the views to that service
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-030, its Data table rows v_ace_account and v_ace_npa_sale); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.21.2 integration points, A2.21.3.1 rule table); Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 slides 8 and 37 (the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views read only by rwb-source-data); _work/msr/context/S5.md (connection matrix row S5 Asset, no P1 column mark; DP-05)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s5 X6 and X9; s11 Data; s12.2; s13; CON s3, s7 AC4, s11 Data, s12.2, s12.7
description: The legacy story reads the balance and the NPA sale facts from v_ace_account and v_ace_npa_sale, and the FSD keeps both entities in the feature. In the target the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views are read only by rwb-source-data, and the connection matrix marks no call and no subscription between S5 and P1, so the step has no declared route to the two facts it needs. DP-05 turns the legacy reads into a contract with the owner or into the service's own ACE views, and the service owns none.
evidence: Legacy Data table: v_ace_account DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042 and v_ace_npa_sale DF-ACE-220 to DF-ACE-230. Architecture v5 slide 8 notes: the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views, read only by rwb-source-data. Connection matrix row S5 Asset: the P1 Source data column is blank. Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-05.
area: Data ownership, S5 rwb-asset with P1 rwb-source-data
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the owner of P1 rwb-source-data
proposed: Read the balance and the NPA sale facts on the rwb-source-data data product, or on the rwb-case case view where the case already carries the balance, keep no v_ace_* grant in rwb_asset, and raise the missing matrix edge and the product shape with the two owners.

title: No table, column or list carries the residual, its route or its hand-off to the D9 decision
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-030, Acceptance criteria AC2 and its Data table); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.21.3.1 rule rows R-DIS-55 and R-DIS-71); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (rows R-DIS-55, R-DIS-57, R-DIS-58 and R-DIS-71); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1 asset_sale and listing, T3.2 lists); _work/msr/context/S5.md (tables owned by S5: asset_sale and listing)
section: APP s1 Story; s3 Preconditions; s4 steps 4, 8 and 9; s8 BR5; s11 Data; s12.1; s12.7; s13; s19; CON s2, s7 AC2, s11 Data, s12.1, s12.7, s13
description: R-DIS-55 fires on shortfall_amount above 0 and R-DIS-71 on a residual_route that is not set, yet no element of the two tables this service owns holds either value. asset_sale carries the price, the two taxes, the fee, incentive_amount and a gain_loss formula, and listing carries the prices and the round; proceeds is P8's. The residual, its route and the D9 hand-off therefore have no home in the target schema, and no source states whether they are a sale element, a case element or a decision record only.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.1 asset_sale fields DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019: no shortfall and no residual route. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-55 condition shortfall_amount above 0; R-DIS-71 condition residual_route is not set; R-DIS-57 and R-DIS-58 route on residual_route = write_off and residual_route = debt_sale. Legacy AC2: raise the residual for the D9 decision. Ownership Map: proceeds owned by P8.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the data model owner and the owner of P7 rwb-decision
proposed: Hold the residual as the outcome of the R-DIS-55 decision record and as the stage outcome answered to rwb-case, compute it from the proceeds fact, the sale record and the rule rows with their versions, add no column in this wave and raise the element request with the data model and case owners.

title: Legacy AC3 applies the proceeds to the loan account while that application is FEAT-PAY-10 of rwb-payment, and R-DIS-54 also names Agent Runtime as a system
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-030, Acceptance criteria AC1 and AC3, metadata Depends on FEAT-PAY-10); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.21.2 integration points ALS and GL, A2.21.3.1 rule table); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (rows FEAT-AST-21 and FEAT-PAY-10); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (row R-DIS-54, its Systems column); _work/msr/context/S5.md (Ownership Map rows of S5 and connection matrix row S5 Asset)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s7 note on AC3; s8 BR3 and the note under the rule table; s12.2; s13; s19; CON s1 Story; s11 Data; s12.2; s19
description: One step is written twice. Legacy AC3 and its Then line apply the proceeds to the case and the loan account, while FEAT-PAY-10 of P8 is described as applying every receipt to the balance in the order the policy sets, and the legacy story names FEAT-PAY-10 as its prerequisite. R-DIS-54 lists ALS core and GL with Agent Runtime as its systems. No source states which service writes the balance application, which service matches the vendor fee, or what the Agent Runtime contributes to this step, and DP-20 is outside the pattern set of the two slices.
evidence: Legacy AC3 Then: apply the proceeds to the case and the loan account, and match the vendor fee. Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3: FEAT-PAY-10 Apply proceeds to the case balance, System, runs unattended, ALS and GL, FEAT-PAY-04. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-54 systems: ALS core and GL, Agent Runtime. Ownership Map: proceeds owned by P8; asset_sale owned by S5.
area: Service boundary, S5 rwb-asset with P8 rwb-payment and P10 rwb-agent
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the owners of P8 rwb-payment and P10 rwb-agent
proposed: Keep the criterion word for word, let rwb-payment apply the money and post it, let rwb-asset evaluate the case side of R-DIS-54, write the sale outcome, match the fee as a fact of the proceeds row and answer the move, and claim no agent call in this wave.

title: The vendor fee that R-DIS-54 matches has no element in S5 and no stated owner of the match
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (row R-DIS-54, action and systems); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1 asset_sale fields DF-SAL-015 to DF-SAL-019); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.21.3.1 rule table); _work/msr/context/S5.md (Ownership Map: proceeds owner P8, asset_sale owner S5)
section: APP s4 step 3; s5 X7; s8 BR6; s11 Data; s12.8; s13; CON s7 AC6, s11 Data, s12.8, s13
description: R-DIS-54 matches the vendor fee, and asset_sale carries transfer_fee, specific_business_tax, corporate_income_tax and incentive_amount without stating which of them is the vendor fee or where the fee of the auction vendor is held. The proceeds row is P8's and its elements are a payment code, a source and an amount. No source states who matches the fee, what a missing match does to the sale outcome, or whether a fee element is written by this service or read from P8.
evidence: R-DIS-54 action: Apply the proceeds to the case and the loan account, and match the vendor fee. TSD S5 T3.1 asset_sale: DF-SAL-015 transfer_fee, DF-SAL-016 specific_business_tax, DF-SAL-017 corporate_income_tax, DF-SAL-019 incentive_amount, with no vendor fee field. Legacy Data table row proceeds: id, case_id, treatment_id, payment_code, source, amount and 3 more.
area: Business rules and data, S5 rwb-asset
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the owner of P8 rwb-payment and the DISPOSAL rule owner in P7
proposed: Read the fee as a fact of the proceeds row, match it against transfer_fee and record the match as the rule outcome, and hold an unmatched fee on the case task without reversing the sale; ask the rule owner to name the fee element at the next rule version.

title: Five rules of the feature own no legacy criterion, so the no-shortfall close, the residual routing and the unmatched exception have no story
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.21.3.1 rule rows R-DIS-55, R-DIS-54, R-DIS-71 and A2.21.4 no alternate flow); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (rows R-DIS-56, R-DIS-57, R-DIS-58, R-DIS-71 and R-DIS-72); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-030, Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4)
section: APP s4 step 9; s5 X10; s8 note under the rule table; s9 State transitions; s19; CON s9, s19
description: The FSD A2.21 rule table carries R-DIS-55, R-DIS-54 and R-DIS-71, and the rule workbook adds R-DIS-56 for no shortfall, R-DIS-57 and R-DIS-58 for the residual handed to write-off or debt sale and R-DIS-72 for the manual decision after an unmatched case. The legacy story owns four criteria and none of them covers those five rows, which nevertheless sit in the states this step produces. The split plan carries no further slice of RWB-E4-030, so the rows have no owning story.
evidence: FSD S5 A2.21.3.1 lists VR-S5-021-1, R-DIS-55, R-DIS-54, R-DIS-71 and BR-S5-021. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-56 PROCEEDS_APPLIED on NO_SHORTFALL to CASE_CLOSED_NO_SHORTFALL; R-DIS-57 and R-DIS-58 SHORTFALL_RAISED on RESIDUAL_ROUTED; R-DIS-71 SHORTFALL_RAISED on RESIDUAL_ROUTED to UNMATCHED_EXCEPTION; R-DIS-72 UNMATCHED_EXCEPTION on MANUAL_DECISION_RECORDED to ASSET_HELD. Plan: RWB-E4-030 has the two slices only.
area: Story coverage, S5 rwb-asset with S7 rwb-writeoff
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the write-off route owner and the programme backlog owner
proposed: Name the five rows as adjacent in both slices, keep the four legacy criteria verbatim, and raise a new story for the no-shortfall close and the residual routing with the write-off route and the backlog owner.

title: The legacy screen states of SCR-22 do not match the holding lists and the states this step produces are case states
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-030, Screen and states table); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.2 LOV-HOLDING and LOV-LISTING); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (rows R-DIS-54 and R-DIS-55)
section: APP s9 State transitions; s15 Screens and states; CON s7 AC2, s15
description: The legacy story gives SCR-22 Asset record the states take-on, held, listed and sold, and SCR-21 Asset list the states loading and list. LOV-HOLDING carries HELD, LISTED, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD, TRANSFERRED and RENTED and has no take-on value, LOV-LISTING carries the listing states, and the states the step produces, PROCEEDS_APPLIED and SHORTFALL_RAISED, are case states of the DISPOSAL machine and not holding states. No source states how the screen shows a holding state and a case state together.
evidence: Legacy screen table: SCR-21 Asset list Loading; list. SCR-22 Asset record Take-on; held; listed; sold. TSD S5 T3.2 LOV-HOLDING: HELD, LISTED, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD, TRANSFERRED, RENTED; LOV-LISTING: DRAFT, LIVE, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD, WITHDRAWN. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-54 to PROCEEDS_APPLIED and R-DIS-55 to SHORTFALL_RAISED.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the screen owner of RWB-PLT-N001 and the case owner of P3
proposed: Show the holding state from LOV-HOLDING and the case state beside it, read take-on as the take-on story's ASSET_ON_BOOKS and ASSET_HELD pair, and leave the legacy wording as the business description of the screen.

title: The slice consumes an event and evaluates a rule package, while DP-09 and DP-04 are outside its pattern set and no platform build row is carried
source: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (both slices, patterns DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19 only, H lists); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-04 and DP-09 rows); Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4 (Rules sheet, outbox and consumers); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (rows R-DIS-54 and R-DIS-55)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s12.4; s12.7; s13; s17; s19; CON s3, s7 AC6 and AC7, s7 note, s12.4, s13, s19
description: The step reads one Kafka event through an inbox and evaluates two Drools rules of the DISPOSAL package, so DP-09 and DP-04 both describe its mechanism, yet the plan fixes the pattern set at DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19 and the H lists carry only the CON slice and the two platform CON stories of DP-03 and DP-19. No source states whether the inbox and the package load add a platform build dependency for this key.
evidence: split_plan.json patterns for both slices: DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19; H of the APP slice: RWB-S5-E4030-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON. Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04 adds H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON; DP-09 adds H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the platform event and workflow owners
proposed: Declare the inbox and the outbox as platform capabilities of the event platform and the package as loaded through the service template, claim no new H row in this wave, and raise the platform dependency question with the platform owners at the next plan revision.
